name: Web Application (3-Tier Architecture)
description: Classic 3-tier web application with frontend, backend API, and database. Demonstrates STRIDE threat modeling for common web architectures.

components.name: User Browser
components.description: End user accessing the application via web browser

components.name: Web Application (React)
components.description: Frontend single-page application serving the UI

components.name: REST API Server
components.description: Backend API handling business logic and data operations

components.name: PostgreSQL Database
components.description: Primary relational database storing application data

components.name: Redis Cache
components.description: In-memory cache for session data and frequently accessed content

threats.title: User Identity Spoofing
threats.description: Attacker attempts to impersonate a legitimate user by stealing or forging authentication tokens (JWT).

threats.title: SQL Injection Attack
threats.description: Attacker injects malicious SQL code through user input to manipulate database queries and access unauthorized data.

threats.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
threats.description: Attacker injects malicious JavaScript into web pages viewed by other users, potentially stealing session tokens or performing unauthorized actions.

threats.title: Insufficient Audit Logging
threats.description: Critical user actions (login, data modification, admin operations) are not logged, making it impossible to trace malicious activity.

threats.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Transit
threats.description: Communication between API and Redis cache is not encrypted, potentially exposing session data or sensitive cached content.

threats.title: Database Credentials in Source Code
threats.description: Database connection strings or credentials stored in source code or configuration files in version control.

threats.title: Rate Limiting Absence
threats.description: API endpoints lack rate limiting, allowing attackers to overwhelm the service with excessive requests.

threats.title: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR)
threats.description: API endpoints expose internal object IDs without proper authorization checks, allowing users to access resources they shouldn't.

threats.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
threats.description: Attacker tricks authenticated user into executing unwanted actions via forged requests.

threats.title: Verbose Error Messages
threats.description: Detailed error messages expose internal system architecture, stack traces, or database structure to attackers.

mitigations.title: Implement Secure JWT Handling
mitigations.description: Use short-lived access tokens (15 min), refresh token rotation, secure HttpOnly cookies, and token revocation list for logout.

mitigations.title: Use Parameterized Queries & ORM
mitigations.description: Always use parameterized queries or a trusted ORM (e.g., Prisma, TypeORM) to prevent SQL injection. Never concatenate user input into SQL.

mitigations.title: Content Security Policy & Output Encoding
mitigations.description: Implement strict CSP headers, sanitize all user input, and encode output appropriately for the context (HTML, JavaScript, URL).

mitigations.title: Comprehensive Audit Logging
mitigations.description: Log all authentication events, authorization failures, data modifications, and admin actions with timestamps, user IDs, and IP addresses.

mitigations.title: Enable Redis TLS Encryption
mitigations.description: Configure Redis to use TLS for all connections. Update application to connect via TLS.

mitigations.title: Use Environment Variables & Secrets Manager
mitigations.description: Store all credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault). Never commit secrets to git.

mitigations.title: Implement Rate Limiting
mitigations.description: Add rate limiting middleware (e.g., express-rate-limit) to all API endpoints. Use tiered limits: 100 req/min per IP for public, 1000 req/min for authenticated.

mitigations.title: Enforce Authorization Checks
mitigations.description: Implement consistent authorization middleware that validates user ownership or permission before accessing any resource. Use object-level permissions.

mitigations.title: CSRF Token Protection
mitigations.description: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookie attribute. Verify origin headers.

mitigations.title: Generic Error Messages
mitigations.description: Return generic error messages to users in production. Log detailed errors server-side only. Never expose stack traces or internal paths.
